'''Abraham Ziv''' ({{Langx|he|אברהם זיו}}; {{Birth date|1940|3|6}}–{{death date and age|2013|3|5|1940|3|6}}) was an Israeli mathematician, known for his contributions to the [[Zero-sum problem]] as one of the discoverers of the [[Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv theorem]].

==Biography==
Abraham Zubkowski (later Ziv) was born in [[Avihayil]] to Haim and Zila Zubkovski. In the 1950s, he changed his surname as part of the widespread [[Hebraization of surnames]] trend. He studied at the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]], where he earned his Ph.D. in mathematics, after receiving his master's degree from [[Harvard University]].

==Academic career==
In 1961, at the age of 21, Ziv proved along with [[Paul Erdős]] and [[Abraham Ginzburg]] the general result that every sequence of <math>2n - 1\ </math> elements of  <math>\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}</math> contains <math>n</math> terms that sum to zero.<ref name="zbmath">{{cite journal |last1=Erdős |first1=Paul |last2=Ginzburg |first2=A. |last3=Ziv |first3=A. |title=A theorem in additive number theory |journal=Bull. Res. Council Israel |volume=10F |pages=41–43 |year=1961 |zbl=0063.00009}}</ref>

In 1972 Ziv was part of the founding team of [[IBM R&D Labs in Israel]], where he stayed until retirement. In his time at IBM he wrote 21 more publications<ref name="54a">{{cite web|url=http://65.54.113.26/Author/2328334/abraham-ziv|title=Abraham Ziv|publisher=65.54.113.26|access-date=2015-01-12|archive-url=https://archive.today/20150117232456/http://65.54.113.26/Author/2328334/abraham-ziv|archive-date=2015-01-17}}</ref> and 6 patents.<ref name="justia">{{cite web|url=http://patents.justia.com/inventor/abraham-ziv|title=Patents by Inventor Abraham Ziv - Justia Patents Database|publisher=patents.justia.com|access-date=2015-01-12}}</ref>
